title: Authoring
description: Writing a product down in Lathe's one language: its records and what every record shares, its domains by capability, their aggregates, use cases, patterns, layers, flows, views, endpoints, tests and open questions, and what a product adds to Lathe through its Product extension. Each of those concepts is an aggregate here, with the rules for writing it, and the format reference shows them all.
notes: The checks that hold records to these rules are designed here, beside the rules; Checking runs them and reports what they find.

title: Checking
description: Running the checks and reporting what they find: each check is one SQL file, a problem names its check and its record, and an error means the workspace is broken while a warning is work still to do. A product adds checks of its own. Checking also keeps the structure checks that find gaps, stale citations and levels of the spec that are the wrong size, and shows every problem on the Checks page and the Dock badge.

title: Exploring
description: Reading a product: its pages at their addresses, the wiki, Graph and Model views side by side, the nav and its folders, quick find, spaces, tabs and the side bar's content. The pages read the product's data, and a record's page also changes it: an edit, a new child or a removal goes through the command layer, as an Agent's writes do, and every change lands in the data files for review in git.

title: Platform
description: What every slice stands on: the app shell and workbench with its panels, commands and keys, themes, the workspace loaded from the data files and reloaded live, the command layer every write goes through, the server and its API's transport, and the desktop app, a window per product folder around the same web app. Platform follows the two app patterns, App code (`LA-PAT-APP-CODE`) and App experience (`LA-PAT-APP-UX`), and holds the standards, stability, accessibility and performance suites that prove them for the whole app.
notes: The desktop app runs three ways: `npm --prefix desktop run dev` for development, which loads the owner's dev server on port 5199 when it serves the opened folder or else one of its own; `npm --prefix desktop start`, which builds Lathe and runs the shell as it ships; and `npm --prefix desktop run pack`, an unsigned macOS app for this Mac. Signed builds, notarizing, auto-update and Windows and Linux builds come later and need the owner's approval to publish.

title: Traceability
description: Following a product's links both ways and counting what is designed, built and proved: coverage per domain and obligation kind, the gaps, the proof still owed, the patterns each domain owes, and the evidence a test's file gives for what it claims. The engine counts it, and the app shows it on the product and domain pages and in each record's Traceability section.
